interfaces.name: Pumble client
interfaces.technology: Web app plus native desktop (Windows, macOS, Linux) and mobile (iOS, Android) clients
interfaces.classification_rationale: The primitive is affordance manipulation of a persistent, navigable representation of workspace state; web, desktop, and mobile share this paradigm, base, and auth, so they form one Interactive interface.

provenance.evidence: Lists first-party apps for iOS, Android, Mac, Windows, Linux, and web.
Desktop app performs the same messaging, administration, and invite actions as the web application.

interfaces.name: Pumble REST API
interfaces.technology: HTTP REST API (api.pumble.com / docs.pumble.com), API-key or OAuth2 token auth
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer explicitly invokes provider-defined operations (messages, channels, users, workspace, calls, files) through structured HTTP requests. The two credential paths share one operation set and base, so they are one interface.

provenance.evidence: API Keys addon generates a key to send messages, reactions, and more via HTTP requests, with the full action list in Swagger.
API Client lists the same REST operation families and references the Pumble API docs at docs.pumble.com.

interfaces.name: Incoming Webhooks
interfaces.technology: HTTP POST of JSON or form payload to a unique per-webhook URL
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer explicitly invokes a single provider-defined post-message operation by POSTing a payload to a Pumble-generated URL; distinct base and credential model make it a separate Programmatic interface from the REST API.

provenance.evidence: Documents posting a message by HTTP POST with a text or attachments payload to a unique incoming-webhook URL under api.pumble.com.

interfaces.name: Pumble Apps event and interaction delivery
interfaces.technology: Signed HTTPS callbacks to a developer-hosted endpoint (events, slash commands, shortcuts, block interactions, view actions)
interfaces.classification_rationale: Pumble initiates the interaction on subscribed or user-triggered events and delivers signed payloads to a consumer-controlled receiver; the shared delivery contract makes this one Event interface.

provenance.evidence: Apps register events and eventSubscriptions.url plus command, shortcut, block-interaction, and view handlers, delivered to an eventsPath endpoint and signed with the app signing secret.

interfaces.name: Pumble AI Assistant addon
interfaces.technology: In-workspace AI assistant messaged directly or by @mention, backed by a connected LLM provider
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer interacts through natural-language messages interpreted by the service, and internal orchestration is not part of the consumer-facing contract, so it is Conversational rather than Agentic.

provenance.evidence: Users communicate with the assistant inside Pumble by direct message or by mentioning it in a channel or group DM, and it responds in a thread.

interfaces.name: Pumble native MCP server
interfaces.technology: Model Context Protocol server hosted at pumble.com, exposing tools and built-in prompts
interfaces.classification_rationale: Capability discovery and selection structure the interaction contract, which is Capability Discovery and Invocation; per the MCP boundary rule this is Agentic rather than Programmatic.

provenance.evidence: States Pumble maintains a native MCP server hosted at pumble.com to connect a workspace to an AI agent, listing available tools and built-in prompts.
